newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June30.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June30.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing and the Media
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Germans get bad marks at the International Advertising Festival in Cannes. British and American competitors took home dozens of prizes, but only two German advertising films won awards. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
FRANKFURT - Young & Rubicam has reportedly held onto the multi-million-mark Wuestenrot account after the account was put up for review. JWT was a finalist for the account. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Springer & Jacoby win advertising account for "TV Today", a twice monthly television guide magazine.
(Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
MUNICH - Deutsche Telekom has to make the German cable TV network available to all interested providers, says Postal Minister Wolfgang Boetsch in an interview with Focus magazine.
(Reuter)
LUDWIGSHAFEN - Deutsche Telekom says it wants to make space available for two more channels on its already crowded cable network. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - Bertelsmann wants Essen's Westdeutsche Allgmeine Zeitung group (WAZ) to take a stake in CLT-Ufa, Europe's largest media group. (Focus)

MUNICH - Demand for shares in ProSieben, which will be floated on July 7, far exceeds supply. A total of 17.5 million preferred shares will be offered for sale. Those interested in ordering ProSieben shares can still place their orders until Thursday. The shares are being offered for between 66 and 72 marks.

FRANKFURT - Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom are planning cross shareholding over the long term. Chief Financial officer Joachim Kroeske tells Reuters Financial TV that there can be no doubt about an exchange in shares over the longer term. He said the decision of the German government to reduce its stake by a further 25 percent created the conditions for a cross shareholding.
PEOPLE NEWS:
DUESSELDORF - E-Plus Mobilfunk AG names Krups manager Klaus Thiemann as new marketing chief, starting September 1. Thiemann will take over the office of deputy chairman. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Former Mercedes-Benz chairman Helmut Werner will take job as supervisory board chairman at Alcatel Holding.
(Focus)

HAMBURG - Siemens calls Der Spiegel report about its plans to restructure corporate leadership speculative. Spiegel says Siemens plans to add telecoms expert Peter Pribilla from supervisory board to managing board, where Pribilla will replace Walter Kunerth. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Daniela Sakowski, the head of publishing at "Werben & Verkaufen" magazine, will leave the Europa-Facpresse-Verlag and Volker Schmitt will take over from July 1. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Hemjoe Klein, 56, a member of Lufthansa's corporate board, was given a contract extension by the supervisory board. Klein is responsible for the group's marketing. (Horizont)
